2. A physically different candidate is covalent carrier-to-carrier handover.

Consider the schematic topology
old-carrier--leaving-group--acyl(prefix) + amine--new-unit--new-carrier
 -> old-carrier--leaving-group + prefix--amide--new-unit--new-carrier.
If actually implemented, the prefix changes its carrier because its new product bond is made; mere release of the old carrier is not the continuation observation. Hydrolysis can instead release a failed prefix without putting it on the next carrier. Correct local docking, the next reactive end, suppression of background reactions, positional register, usable chemical functionality, activation and carrier renewal remain actual construction problems.
